text:
alex: Heads-up — discovered a weird interaction with nested modals + toasts in the console. Repro: open Workspace modal -> open 'Edit route' modal on top -> trigger a toast (save success) while the top modal resizes content. Focus sometimes jumps to the toast and ESC closes the toast but then immediately closes the top modal too.

alex: I can repro on Chrome + Safari, desktop and narrow width. Screenshot + short screencap attached (gfycat link).

mica: oof. Does this only happen when the top modal changes height after the toast appears?

alex: Seems correlated. If top modal height changes (dynamic list loads), focus restore code tries to move focus back to the previously focused element but the toast grabs focus briefly. If ESC pressed while toast has focus, our global handler bubbles and closes the modal stack.

jon: Are we relying on a single document-level ESC listener rather than per-modal focus-trap listeners? IIRC we had a global `keydown: escape` to close top modal id.

tara: For accessibility we should ensure toasts are non-focusable by default unless they contain interactive controls. Are these toasts focusable in the repro?

alex: The toast has a dismiss button (x) so the container gets focus in our implementation (we `focus()` the toast to announce it). Might be the wrong approach.

ben: Options I can think of: 1) never programmatically focus toasts — rely on `aria-live` instead; 2) if we must focus toasts, make ESC only close toasts when toast is focused and stopPropagation on the toast's ESC handler; 3) ensure modal focus-restore runs after toast lifecycle completes (race fix).

mica: Preference towards aria-live (1) + explicit focusable dismiss button inside for keyboard users. That avoids stealing focus from the modal.

jon: Implementation notes: our current focus-restore code does: `previouslyFocusedElem?.focus()` in the toast success callback. Could change order or add a microtask delay. Also we have a single `document.addEventListener('keydown', onEsc)` in ModalManager which closes the top modal without checking `event.target` or `event.defaultPrevented` — that's risky.

tara: Ideally top-level ESC should query `closest('[data-focus-trap]')` or check `event.target` to see if an interactive element (like a toast dismiss) is focused, then defer to that element's handler. Also ensure to use `aria-live="polite"` on toasts for announcements.

ben: Quick patch suggestion: stop programmatic toast focus, add `role="status" aria-live="polite"` to the toast container, keep the dismiss button tabbable. Also change ModalManager ESC handler to ignore ESC if `document.activeElement` is inside an element with `data-toast` attribute.

alex: I'll prototype two quick branches: `no-toast-focus` (aria-live) and `esc-guard` (guard ESC by activeElement). I'll link PRs once ready.

jon: Heads-up for runtime team: if we change ESC handler semantics, check any existing code relying on global ESC to cancel flows (release notes?). Might be minor but worth flagging.

ci-bot: new commit pushed to alex/no-toast-focus (a1b2c3). CI: tests/keyboard focus coverage updated.

mica: Thanks — can we add a small acceptance test: nested modal -> trigger toast -> press ESC -> top modal remains open and toast closes? If so, ship. :+1:

ben: Also add a small note in the component docs about toasts using aria-live and not stealing focus.

alex: Yep. I'll add test and doc copy. Will update thread when PRs are up.

tara: Nice. Also let's run this past accessibility review after patch. I can take that.

alex: Cool — assigning to @tara for a11y review once PR is ready.
